questions.q:
The ratio $\frac{K_P}{K_C}$ for the reaction
$\mathrm{CO}_{(\mathrm{g})}+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2(\mathrm{ g})} \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CO}_{2(\mathrm{ g})}$ is:
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_2(\mathrm{ g}) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CO}_2(\mathrm{ g})\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}}$ and $\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}$ are related as
$\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}}=\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}(\mathrm{RT})^{\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}}\Rightarrow \quad \Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}=\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{P}}-\mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{R}}=1-1 \frac{1}{2}=-\frac{1}{2}\Delta \mathrm{n}_{\mathrm{g}}$ for the given reaction $=-\frac{1}{2}\therefore \frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{RT}}}$

questions.q: For an isomerisation reaction $A \rightleftharpoons B$, the temperature dependence of equilibrium constant is given by $\log _e K=4.0-\frac{2000}{T}$ The value of $\Delta S^{{}^{\circ}}$ at Hook is, therefore
questions.solution: van't Hoff equation giving variation of equilibrium constant, $K$ with temperature $T$ is $\log _e K=-\frac{\Delta H^{{}^{\circ}}}{R T}+\frac{\Delta S^{{}^{\circ}}}{R}$ Given, $\quad \log _e K=-\frac{2000}{T}+4.0\therefore \quad \Delta S^{{}^{\circ}} / R=4 \Rightarrow \Delta S^{{}^{\circ}}=4 R$

questions.q: The ratio $\frac{K_{p}}{K_{c}}$ for the reaction $\mathrm{CO}(g)+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}(g) \rightleftharpoons \mathrm{CO}_{2}(g)$ is:
questions.solution: $K_{P}=K_{C}(R T)^{\Delta n_{\text{g }}}$ For the reaction $\mathrm{CO}(\mathrm{g})+\frac{1}{2} \mathrm{O}_{2}(g) \leftrightharpoons \mathrm{CO}_{2}(\mathrm{ g})\Delta n_{g}=1-\left(1+\frac{1}{2}\right)=-\frac{1}{2}\therefore \quad \mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}}=\frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}}{\sqrt{\mathrm{RT}}} ; \quad \frac{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{P}}}{\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{C}}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{RT}}}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An equilibrium mixture at $300K$ contains ${N}_{2}{O}_{4}$ and ${NO}_{2}$ at $0. 28$ and $1. 1atm$ pressure, respectively. If the volume of the container is doubled, the new equilibrium pressure of these two gases are respectively.
questions.solution:
${N}_{2}{O}_{4}\left(g\right) ⇌ 2{NO}_{2}\left(g\right)$

Pressure at equilibrium
${K}_{p} = {p}_{{NO}_{2}}^{2}{p}_{{N}_{2}{O}_{4}} = \dfrac{{\left(1 . 1\right)}^{2}}{0 . 28} = 4 . 32atm$

If volume of the container is doubled, the pressure will reduced to half

${N}_{2}{O}_{4} ⇌ 2{N}_{2}O$

New pressure,

$\left[\dfrac{0 . 028}{2} - p\right]\left[\dfrac{1 . 1}{2} + 2p\right]$

${K}_{p} = \dfrac{{\left[\dfrac{1 . 1}{2} + 2p\right]}^{2}}{\left[\dfrac{0 . 28}{2} - p\right]} = 4 . 32$

On solving, we get

$p = 0 . 045$

$∴ {p}_{{N}_{2}{O}_{4}} = 0 . 14 - 0 . 045 = 0 . 095atm$

${p}_{{NO}_{2}} = 0 . 55 + \left(2 \times 0 . 045\right) = 0 . 64atm$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following according to LeChatelier's principle is correct?
options: Increase in temperature favours the endothermic reaction
Increase in temperature favours the exothermic reaction
Increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium in that side in which number of gaseous moles increases
All of the above are true
questions.solution: According to Le-Chatelier's principle increase in temperature favours the endothermic reaction while decrease in temperature favour the exothermic reaction. Increase in pressure shifts the equilibrium in that side in which number of gaseous moles decreases.
